[[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2012 AP & Sporting News 3rd team All-American]] }} {{MedalTableTop}} {{MedalSport | Men’s [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 World Championship|FIBA U19 World Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2009 Auckland]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} {{MedalBottom}} '''Tyshawn Jamar Taylor''' (born April 6, 1990) is an American [[Basketball|basketball]] player who currently plays for the [[University of Kansas]].[http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taylor_tyshawn00.html KUathletics.com Profile] ==High school== Taylor attended [[St. Anthony High School (New Jersey)|St. Anthony High School]] in New Jersey where he played under renowned high-school coach [[Bob Hurley]]. During the 2007-08 season Taylor's team went 32-0 and was awarded the high school basketball [[mythical national championship]] by [[USA Today]]. Taylor also appeared in the 2009 film ''The Street Stops Here'', a documentary about Hurley and St. Anthony[http://www.imdb.com/title/tt1162126/ The Street Stops Here - IMDB]. ===Freshman year=== Taylor averaged 7.2 pts, 3.4 assists per game on the [[2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team]] who won both the Big 12 regular season and tournament championships. Taylor was voted 2010 Big 12 Freshman of the year. ===Sophomore year=== Taylor averaged 9.3 points and 4.6 assists his sophomore year. Taylor led the team in assists and was fourth in the Big 12. On February 21, 2011, Taylor was suspended indefinitely from the team for violating team rules. The specifics of the suspension were not announced..http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6144510 ===Senior Year=== Starting for the fourth straight year, Taylor nearly doubled his career scoring average. Taylor, along with all-american [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], helped lead Kansas to the national championship before losing to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. ==US Under-19 Team== Taylor represented [[USA Basketball]] as they won the [[FIBA Under-19 World Championship 2009|2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. Taylor averaged a team-high 10.8 points and a team-high 4.4 assists per game.[http://newzealand2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/u19men/player/p/pid/76839/sid/4034/tid/379/accumulated-statistics.html USA Basketball - Taylor Stats] His team-high 18 points and 6 assists in the final game against Greece helped secure the championship for the United states.[http://newzealand2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/u19men/p/gid/A/grid/62/rid/6982/game.html USA Break Gold Medal Drought In Style] After the tournament, Taylor was named to the five-person All-Star team for the tournament along with teammate [[Gordon Hayward]].[http://newzealand2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/u19men/news/p/eid/4034/nid/30987/sid/4034/article.html The Best of the Best Selected] ==See also== * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball players with 145 games played]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Persondata | NAME = Taylor, Tyshawn | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = April 6, 1991 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Hoboken, NJ]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Taylor, Tyshawn}} [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Jersey]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[ru:Тейлор, Тишон]]
